source: Royal Government of Cambodia, General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA) / Boosting Food Production Program (PMO), "ខែ្សសង្វាក់ផលិតកម្ម ដំណាំពោតនៅកម្ពុជា" (Corn Production Value Chain in Cambodia), 2017
text:
A household survey covering 250 red-corn growing households was conducted across four provinces: Kampong Cham (53 households), Kandal (73), Battambang (69), and Pailin (55).

Of the 250 household heads interviewed, 45% (113) were men and 55% (137) were women, though this reflects who answered the survey (often the wife), not necessarily who leads farm decisions -- 42% of households said decisions are made by the husband and 50% by the wife, with the rest made jointly or by other family members. Households averaged 4.96 members, of which an average of 2.41 were female and 3.26 were under 18 years old.

Education levels of household heads: 19% (47) had no schooling; 43% (108) had primary education; 27% (67) had lower-secondary education; 10% (25) had upper-secondary/high-school education; and 1% (3) had university education.

Regarding land tenure of the household's residential land: 84% (209) obtained their homestead land through inheritance, and 16% (41) purchased it. Of those who purchased, 8% bought it within their current commune and 7% bought it from elsewhere. Reasons for moving/settling included following relatives (7%), following a spouse's family (4%), for farm work (3%), and for other economic opportunity (2%). Regarding occupation: all surveyed households farm, 20% also raise livestock, 14% do wage labor, and 6% do other trading.
